Necromancy.name: Necromancy
Necromancy.description:
That life and death need not be in direct opposition

The study of life, death and undeath has long fascinated scholars of magic, so naturally, certain practitioners of the arts have focused exclusively on it. Though the most well-known of necromancers are dreaded for raising the dead as armies of monsters, there exist just as many who argue that necromancy is not an inherently evil subject, and that only through studying the undead (and by commanding animated motes of void energy shaped to look like true undead) can we prepare ourselves for the horrors that await the world. Necromancers of the School of Civic Wizardry may be catacomb designers or gravekeepers innovating their craft, while those of the School of Aetheral Astrologia may be seeking a way to infuse the vital power of stars into their creations.

Your deliberation skill is Medicine. When you attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Q5iIYCFdqJFM31GW]{Learn a Spell} you must use a corpse, bones, or other remnants of the deceased to produce the vellum, pages, or sigils for your spellbook which you harness with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.s1vB3HdXjMigYAnY]{Healer's Toolkit}. These remnants do not need to be from a sapient creature, so long as the creature was once alive. The remnants must be from a creature of a level at least twice the rank of the spell you are attempting to learn and you cannot use remnants from the same creature more than once, otherwise your attempt to Learn a Spell automatically fails.

Your intrinsic bond to magic is through biological matter which no longer teems with life or soul. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-wizards.wizards-misc.o0QMw5sUYexhLvZi]{Divest Soul} action.

Stance: Consult Tome.name: Stance: Consult Tome
Stance: Consult Tome.description:
Requirements You are holding your spellbook.

The spellbook is a powerful tool with invaluable notes locked within, and when you set your mind to scouring its pages for a trusted spell you are able to replicate it without preparation. During your daily preparations, select a number of spells equal to half your Intelligence modifier to be selectable as your Consulted Spells. If you are at least 10th level, you can select a number of spells equal to your Intelligence modifier instead.

When you enter this stance, you choose a creature, haunt, or object as your target and one of your Consulted Spells. The spell becomes your Consulted Spell. You can expend a separate prepared spell slot of any rank you have to cast your Consulted Spell, heightening to the expended spell’s rank, but you must include the target in your spell’s effects when you Cast the Spell. You are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the beginning of your next turn when you Cast a Spell in this way as you glance back at your notes frequently.

Simulacrous Casting.name: Simulacrous Casting
Simulacrous Casting.description:
You and your clone perform an action at your behest. Either you or your clone Casts a Spell using the same number of actions as Simulcrous Casting, and the other takes a single action. For example, if you spent 2 actions Simulcrous Casting, you could cast breath fire (2 actions) and your clone could Recall Knowledge (1 action), or your clone could cast breath fire (2 actions) and you could Stride (1 action).

This lets you each use separate exploration activities when spellcasting is involved, such as Repeat a Spell as you travel. You can also perform the Learn a Spell activity or perform research in half the normal amount of time, provided you and your clone work in close proximity.

Special If you or your clone use a spellshape and your next action is to use Simulacrous Casting, the spellshape applies to the spell you or your clone casts as part of Simulacrous Casting so long as it would apply to the spell.

Dueling Wand.name: Dueling Wand
Dueling Wand.description:
Requirements You successfully made a spell attack roll in the last round while holding your makeshift wand and are still holding it.

You use your wand to direct attacks to be more precise with a flourish. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that would require a spell attack roll, you gain a +1 status bonus to your spell attack roll. If the spell has multiple targets, the status bonus applies to all of them. If you are at least 10th level, the status bonus increases to +2, and if you are at least 18th level the status bonus increases to +3.

For the duration, when you successfully Aid an ally on a Strike against the creature you allow them to target vital areas, dealing 1 additional precision damage.

Heightened (+1) The precision damage increases by 1.

Dimensional Jump.name: Dimensional Jump
Dimensional Jump.description:
Cost Expend a spell slot

You know how to tear the fabric of reality so that you can hop through time and space through magic. You create portals that allow you to teleport to a place you can see within 5 feet plus an additional 5 feet per rank of the spell you expended.

Rebuttal r Trigger You Step; Effect You create a portal at the end of your Step, teleporting you in the same direction of your Step.

Unravel 3 (manipulate) You make a series of portal jumps in succession, allowing you to move quickly with little risk. You Step, creating a portal and teleporting up to the specified distance and can then use a single action of your choice. After you complete the action, you can then Step back through the portal you created, immediately returning to your previous location. Each Step must be made on a solid surface.

Spell Effect: Rider/Swordsman.description: +1 status bonus to melee attack rolls and Perception

Cryptomancy.name: Cryptomancy
Cryptomancy.description:
That the arcane is inherently unknowable

Certain wizards subscribe to the theory that magic is, by definition, totally abstruse. Every new discovery by magical scholars unearths dozens of new questions, and it is the theory of the cryptomancer–commonly known as a beguiler– that this is by design. Beguilers focus on the unknowable aspects of magic; the threads of the energies that connect planes, bind curses, and forge tangible bonds. Certain beguilers aim to use cryptomancy to hide the most dire secrets of the world; others are dedicated to using this obscure mysticism to uncover the truth. A beguiler of the School of Battle Magic might focus on magic as a tool of subterfuge and intrigue to spy, while a beguiler from the School of Mentalism is more likely one dedicated to seeking out the most forbidden of lost secrets. Regardless of your school, your magic is shrouded in secrets, drawn from the seams between the folds of the tangible, and your methods for learning are adapted from cryptic methods.

Your deliberation skill is Deception. When others attempt to Learn a Spell from you, they must first attempt a check with the skill against your Deception DC. Creatures that fail this check get an automatic failure on their attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Q5iIYCFdqJFM31GW]{Learn a Spell}.

Your intrinsic bond to magic is a cipher only you understand, a phrase, cryptograph, secret sigil, or cloaking technique through which you funnel your magic. You gain @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-wizards.wizards-misc.JkjlQTGobdi1erT7]{Cloaked Casting}.

Dynamancy.name: Dynamancy
Dynamancy.description:
That the body is just as vital as the mind in spellcraft

There are some who are born with an innate magic, and it is from their bodies that their magic springs forth. While you are far from a sorcerer, you have also come to store your magic within yourself through heavily disciplined exercise. Affectionately nicknamed “muscle wizards” in some parts of the world, you use the proper term of dynamancer, or more likely, vitalist.

Unlike most of their kin, vitalists are exceptionally athletic, balancing the academic and the aerobic in perfect tandem, and boosting them beyond what others dream of accomplishing. Vitalists hold that a disciplined body is key to disciplined magic, and they study both in tandem to make your casting perfect. Vitalists of the School of Ars Grammatica may use their body to execute precise movements which mimic the power points of runes far more effectively, while a vitalist of the School of Protean Form may experiment in magic to further bolster their physique in ways many would balk at.

Your deliberation skill is Athletics. You do not use a spellbook to prepare spells, instead storing everything you learn mentally–a feat only possible thanks to your enhanced exercise regiment. You gain a mnemonic bank of spells that exist solely within your own mind, but otherwise functions as a spellbook for abilities and feats which would require you to use a spellbook. Others cannot @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Q5iIYCFdqJFM31GW]{Learn a Spell} from you unless they also succeed at an Athletics check against the DC to Learn the Spell to perform the basic exercises associated with your spell.

Your intrinsic bond to magic is through your body and your strict physical routine to strengthen the connection to magic. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-wizards.wizards-misc.MDf0fgWz9tCwJqg7]{Arcane Vitalization} stance.

Spell Effect: Summon Jury (Call to Order.description:
Arrive (emotion, mental) Call to Order The target must attempt a will save as you charge them with accusation.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes a –1 status penalty to its next attack roll for 1 round.

Failure The target takes a –1 status penalty to all attack rolls for 1 round.

Critical Failure The target takes a –1 status penalty to attack rolls and to its save against the Depart effect.

Residual Energy Capture.name: Residual Energy Capture
Residual Energy Capture.description:
Trigger You Cast a Spell from your wizard spell slots with the acid, air, cold, earth, electricity, fire, metal, water, or wood traits or that would summon a creature with one of these traits.

You claim some of the residual elements of your spell to repurpose them for kinetic energy. You gain residual energy, an effect that lasts for 1 minute with the same trait as the triggering spell. You can choose to expend your residual energy when you cast a spell from your spell slots that would deal damage of the same type as your residual energy to deal additional damage equal to the triggering spell’s rank. You lose your residual energy if you're knocked out or you Dismiss this effect. If you use Residual Energy Capture while you already have residual energy, you lose and regain residual energy for a trait appropriate for the triggering spell.

Effect: Adaptable Energy.name: Effect: Adaptable Energy
Effect: Adaptable Energy.description: You grant resistance to the damage type that matches the energy trait of the expended spell equal to twice the spell’s rank to the target or area.

Spell Effect: Thrush/Swallow.description: +15-foot status bonus to all Speeds

Cloaked Casting.name: Cloaked Casting
Cloaked Casting.description:
When you target a single enemy with one of your wizard spells and the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to you, they also take a –1 circumstance penalty to their saves or you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your spell attack rolls against them. If you are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.1wQY3JYyhMYeeV2G]{Observed} by a creature, and you Cast a Spell that takes 3 actions or less to cast, you do not lose the concealed, hidden, undetected, or unobserved condition until after the spell is cast if you would lose the condition from Casting the Spell.

Special If you are a wizard of the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classfeatures.xYYhJtGhFSWNifcO]{School of Unified Magical Theory}, when you Cast a Spell from one of your wizard spell slots against an off-guard creature and the creature fails its save or you succeed at your spell attack roll, you do not expend the spell slot. You can only gain this effect once for each rank of spells you can cast per day.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-wizards.wizards-misc.Item.WQxHsROxfhxUwTl6]{Effect: Cloaked Casting}

Animatamancy.name: Animatamancy
Animatamancy.description:
That all objects contain a spark and can facilitate life

The history of animating objects—from giant statues to silverware—goes back to the golden age of Nex. The biggest proponents of the art, named imbuers, argue fervently that to expend spell slots in flashy explosions is (while sometimes necessary) nowhere near as useful as the animation of the inanimate. They spend hours designing and then animating the perfect tools for everyday life and—occasionally—for adventuring too. An imbuer of the School of Planar Jurisprudence might be focused on perfecting autonomous security forces or courts, while one attending the School of Penumbral Sculpture might specialize in casting long distinctive shadows. The one thing in common between imbuers is their goal to make every day tasks take care of themselves, to give more time to the world to focus on other pursuits.

Your deliberation skill is Crafting. You do not gain a traditional spell book but instead collect sparks of life within items of magical nature, which you add to your spark collection. Your spark collection doubles as a formula book. When you attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Q5iIYCFdqJFM31GW]{Learn a Spell}, you must break down a magical item with a level at least twice the rank of the spell you are attempting to learn to find its spark. If you are successful, you add the spark to your collection and the item gains the broken condition, but can be Repaired as normal. You cannot use the same object more than once for the Learn a Spell activity, as once you have added a spark to your collection it cannot produce another. Your intrinsic magical bond is to your spark collection. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-wizards.wizards-misc.hohuWXsWCSFmvdsr]{Animated Spark} focus cantrip.

Deploy Worldsphere.name: Deploy Worldsphere
Deploy Worldsphere.description:
You bring everyone into your world by dropping a worldsphere onto the floor and allowing it to shatter. You create a @Template[type:burst|distance:60] within 30 feet that follows your worldsphere’s rules. You select the rules from the following options, though all aesthetic choices are your own. A worldsphere lasts until 1 day has passed, or you Dismiss the effect.

  • Gravity You choose the gravity of your worldsphere, such as zero gravity, high gravity or subjective gravity (giving floating masses their own gravitational pull). High gravity gives creatures @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} unless they are incorporeal, and zero gravity gives creatures the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} conditions and they cannot take move actions unless it is the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.cS9nfDRGD83bNU1p]{Fly} action but can Interact to push off of objects or surfaces to move 10 feet in a direction of their choice.

  • Landmass You can create walls, pits, mesas or even floating platforms within the worldsphere. You can designate up to 30 squares within the worldsphere as raised, lowered or floating. This causes the square to raise or lower by up to 25 feet, or for a floating space to expand its space by 5 feet. You can select a space multiple times to increase this by a further 5 feet.

  • Substances You can fill up to 15 squares with substances such as acid, fire, ice, lava, or water. If the substance would be harmful, it is treated as hazardous terrain that deals 20 damage each time the creature passes through the space or ends its turn in the area of a type appropriate for the terrain.

  • Weather You choose the temperature of your worldsphere, up to incredible cold or heat except creatures take the effects immediately as well as after the duration has elapsed. You also choose whether the area has rain, fog, or is storming, granting concealment to all creatures within the area. You can ignore the severe temperatures and concealment of your worldsphere.

Spell Effect: View Internal Anatomy.name: Spell Effect: View Internal Anatomy
Spell Effect: View Internal Anatomy.description:
You deal 1 additional precision damage on your Strikes and spell attack rolls that deal damage.

Arcane Vitalization.name: Arcane Vitalization
Arcane Vitalization.description:
Requirements Your last action was to Cast a Spell. You need to meet this requirement only to enter the stance, not to remain in it.

With some precise aerobic motions, you harness some of your spell’s energy. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier. The only Strikes you can make are force punch unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 force damage; are in the brawling group; and have the force, parry, shove, trip, and unarmed traits. Alternatively, you can make ranged force punch unarmed attacks out to a range of 30 feet that deal 1d4 force damage with the force, propulsive, and unarmed traits. You can choose to use your spell attack modifier instead of your unarmed attack modifier when you make an attack roll with these attacks, but you do not gain item bonuses to your attack rolls when you do unless they would also apply to your spell attack modifier.

While in Arcane Vitalization, you gain a +3 item bonus to AC and a +1 circumstance bonus to any defenses against being Shoved or Tripped. However, you have a Dexterity modifier cap to your AC of +1, and your Speeds are all reduced by 5 feet. The item bonus to AC from Arcane Vitalization is cumulative with armor potency runes on your explorer's clothing or cloth armors, mystic armor, and bracers of armor. If the spell you Cast to enter this stance was at least a 3rd-rank spell, the item bonus to AC increases to +4.

Special If you are a wizard of the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classfeatures.xYYhJtGhFSWNifcO]{School of Unified Magical Theory}, you regain the spell slot you harnessed if you hit with a melee force punch Strike, critically hit with a ranged force punch Strike, or succeed at a hard or greater DC Athletics check during a non-trivial encounter while under the effects of Arcane Vitalization. You can only gain this effect once for each rank of spells you can cast per day.

Simulacric Sanctuary.name: Simulacric Sanctuary
Simulacric Sanctuary.description:
Trigger You would gain the dying condition or be slain

Requirements You are within 10 miles of your dormant clone

You transfer your mind and affects to your clone in the face of death. You transfer your consciousness and all invested magic items to the destination of your clone, awakening as in the body of your dormant clone immediately. Your body and the body of any other clones you have manifested immediately fall dead as if you had been slain by the triggering effect.

Spell Effect: Animated Spark.name: Spell Effect: Animated Spark
Spell Effect: Animated Spark.description:
Apply this effect to familiars created by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-wizards.wizards-misc.hohuWXsWCSFmvdsr]{Animated Spark}

The target has the same base statistics as a familiar for your level, with the exception of its abilities. It has the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.familiar-abilities.5eqcXtPsYunphMOZ]{Construct} familiar ability, but doesn’t require the tough pet ability. It has a weakness equal to your level to an appropriate damage type, usually bludgeoning, piercing, slashing, or fire unless there would be a more appropriate damage type (subject to GM discretion).

Effect: Immortality Clause.description: You gain 10 resistance to all damage, 20 temporary Hit Points, and regeneration 20 for 1 minute.

Split Spell.description: You know how to splice magic when in a pinch. Choose a prepared spell from spell slots you could have split with Spell Splitter. You can spend 10 minutes to split the spell slot into 2 spells of at least 2 ranks lower than the spell you chose that must share at least 1 trait other than the concentrate or manipulate trait with the chosen spell.

Spell Effect: Wagon/Ox.description: +1 status bonus to Athletics and to saves against forced movement

Spell Effect: Patriarch/Ogre.description: +1 status bonus to Intimidation and to saves against fear

Effect: Powerful Sparks.description:
Apply this effect instead of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-wizards.wizards-misc.NV11EixdATjwYgFo]{Spell Effect: Animated Spark} to your familiar after taking this feat.

Your minions from animated spark lose their weakness and gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.familiar-abilities.Le8UWr5BU8rV3iBf]{Tough} pet ability. In addition, they increase their existing Speeds by 10 feet.

Effect: Superior Wiles.description: The circumstance penalty increases to a –2 circumstance penalty.

Effect: Cloaked Casting.description: When you target a single enemy with one of your wizard spells and the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to you, they also take a –1 circumstance penalty to their saves.

Spell Effect: Shine Spotlight.name: Spell Effect: Shine Spotlight
Spell Effect: Shine Spotlight.description: While a creature is in the spotlight, it has a +1 status bonus to checks to Perform and a –1 circumstance penalty to Stealth checks. Creatures inside the spotlight can spend a single action to @Check[type:performance|defense:will]{Perform} to Sustain the spell on your behalf, and if the creature’s Perform result exceeds the Will DC of a creature outside the spotlight and within 15 feet of the burst, the creature becomes fascinated with the performer and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for as long as it is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated}.

Spell Effect: Mother/Sea Dragon.name: Spell Effect: Mother/Sea Dragon
Spell Effect: Mother/Sea Dragon.description: +1 status bonus to Acrobatics and basic saves

Spell Effect: Darkness Form.name: Spell Effect: Darkness Form
Spell Effect: Darkness Form.description:
You allow elemental shadow to merge with your body, becoming a living shadow. You transform into a Medium battle form that resembles yourself as an elongated shadow, traveling over floors and walls as your own shadow might. While in this form, you gain the incorporeal trait and you can take the Hide action even while being observed in dim light or darkness. You can Dismiss the spell. You gain the following statistics and abilities:

  • AC = 18 + your level. Ignore your armor's check penalty and Speed reduction.

  • 10 temporary Hit Points.

  • Darkvision

  • Resistance to all damage equal to half the spell’s rank

  • A shadowy hand unarmed melee strike, which is the only attack you can Strike with. Your attack modifier is +16, and you deal 2d6 void damage with shadowy hand Strikes. These attacks are Dexterity-based (for the purpose of the clumsy condition, for example). If your attack modifier for Dexterity-based unarmed attacks is higher, you can use it instead.

  • Acrobatics and Stealth modifier of +16, unless your own is higher.

Heightened (5th) You instead gain AC = 19 + your level, 15 temporary HP, an attack modifier of +18, a damage bonus of +5, double the damage dice, Acrobatics +21, and Stealth +21.

Heightened (7th) Your battle form can be up to Large in size and your attacks have 10-foot reach if you are at least Large. You instead gain AC = 21 + your level, 20 temporary HP, resistance to all damage equal to the spell’s rank, an attack modifier of +24, a damage bonus of +15, double the damage dice, Acrobatics +25, and Stealth +25.

Heightened (9th) Your battle form can be up to Huge in size and your attacks have 10-foot reach if you are at least Large, and 15-foot reach if you are Huge.You instead gain AC = 24 + your level, 30 temporary HP, resistance to all damage equal to the spell’s rank, an attack modifier of +29, a damage bonus of +25, triple the damage dice, Acrobatics +29, and Stealth +29.

Effect: Residual Energy.name: Effect: Residual Energy
Effect: Residual Energy.description: You can choose to expend your residual energy when you cast a spell from your spell slots that would deal damage of the same type as your residual energy to deal additional damage equal to the triggering spell’s rank. You lose your residual energy if you're knocked out or you Dismiss this effect. If you use Residual Energy Capture while you already have residual energy, you lose and regain residual energy for a trait appropriate for the triggering spell.

Effect: Fickle Fate.name: Effect: Fickle Fate
Effect: Fickle Fate.description: Affected creatures gain a status bonus to misfortune checks or status penalties to fortune checks equal to 2 plus half the rank of the spell.

Spell Effect: Summon Jury (Verdict).name: Spell Effect: Summon Jury (Verdict)
Spell Effect: Summon Jury (Verdict).description:
Depart (emotion, mental) Verdict The jury renders a verdict on the target, and they must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes a –1 status penalty to its next saving throw for 1 round.

Failure The target takes a –1 status penalty to saving throws for 1 round.

Critical Failure The target is condemned for its crimes and takes a –1 status penalty to saving throws for 1 minute.

Spell Effect: Instant Surgery.name: Spell Effect: Instant Surgery
Spell Effect: Instant Surgery.description:
Critical Success Select two attributes of the target and choose to boost or deplete them. All rolls made with these attributes gain a +1 or –1 status bonus or penalty, depending on your choice.

Success As critical success, but one attribute must be a +1 status boost, and one must be a –1 status penalty.

Quasiplanar Spellcasting.name: Quasiplanar Spellcasting
Quasiplanar Spellcasting.description:
You can tear open minor fluxes to the planes, drawing in power and magic to serve your means. You gain additional spell slots and a spell repertoire from your studied planes. At first level, you can cast one 1st-rank fusion spell per day. You must have the spell in your fusion spell repertoire to cast it; this is a collection of spells granted to you by all of your studied planes. Any of these spells that aren’t normally on the arcane list are still arcane spells if you cast them this way. As you increase in level, you gain further fusion spell slots, and your studied planes grant you higher-rank fusion spells, as detailed in each planar entry.

Heightening Spells

When you gain spell slots of 2nd rank and higher, you can fill those slots with stronger versions of lower-rank spells. This increases the spell’s rank, heightening it to match the spell slot. Many spells have specific improvements when they are heightened to certain ranks.

Your fluxes however can reprocess your magical power into any vessel based on their location. All of your fusion spells are signature spells. That means that you can heighten a fusion spell freely by casting it from a higher-rank fusion spell slot, up to the maximum rank of fusion spell you can cast.

Animated Spark.name: Animated Spark
Animated Spark.description:
With a wave of your hand, you repurpose the sparks of magic to animate mundane objects around you to best suit your needs, and give the resulting creation life. The target becomes a semi-sentient creature with the minion trait that gains 2 actions when you Cast the Spell and when you Sustain the spell to give it commands. The target objects must not be magical, consumable, or otherwise complex (subject to GM discretion). If you Cast the Spell on another target, the spell automatically ends.

The target has the same base statistics as a familiar for your level, with the exception of its abilities. It has the construct familiar ability, but doesn’t require the tough pet ability. It has a weakness equal to your level to an appropriate damage type, usually bludgeoning, piercing, slashing, or fire unless there would be a more appropriate damage type (subject to GM discretion). The creature has 2 pet abilities in addition to its construct ability chosen at the time of casting and the target must meet any prerequisites for the ability selection.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-wizards.wizards-misc.NV11EixdATjwYgFo]{Spell Effect: Animated Spark}

The target can disperse itself as a single action, dealing 2d4 damage in a 5-foot emanation with a basic Reflex save against your spell DC. This damage is bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (as appropriate for the object). After it disperses itself, the objects become inanimate again and the spell ends. If you choose not to Sustain the spell, the spell does not automatically end so long as the last command you gave the target could be repeated exactly, gaining a single action to complete its task at the end of each of your turns. If the target cannot reasonably perform the last task you gave it (subject to GM discretion), it spends a single action to disperse itself instead.

If you already have a familiar, these creatures do not count towards your limit of having a familiar. If you are at least 11th level, you can select familiar abilities (but not master abilities) instead of pet abilities, but you can never select the spellcasting familiar ability for the target of this spell.

Heightened (+1) You increase the maximum Bulk of the targets by 1, and the damage increases by 1d4.

Special If you are a wizard of the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classfeatures.xYYhJtGhFSWNifcO]{School of Unified Magical Theory}, you create a number of separate familiars as you have ranks of spells, provided there are enough objects you could target within range. Each familiar can have different abilities. Only one familiar can be dispersed each round and if multiple familiars would be dispersed as a result of having no action, they become inanimate without dispersing.

Steal Spell.name: Steal Spell
Steal Spell.description:
Requirements Your last action was to Cast a Spell from spell slots that targeted at least one creature within 30 feet.

By expelling magic, you can siphon some in return from the creature. Attempt a Thievery check against the Will DC of the required creature using your Intelligence modifier instead of your Dexterity modifier for your check. Alternatively you can target a willing creature without needing to meet the requirements by touching them and they can choose to grant you the effects of a success.

If you target a creature that does not have the ability to Cast a Spell that would appear on your spell list, the target is instead your choice of enfeebled 1 or stupefied 1 until the end of your next turn on a success instead of the normal effects. Regardless of the result, the target becomes temporarily immune until your next daily preparations.

Success You steal a spell from the target that appears in the arcane tradition. Choose a cantrip or spell of a rank you can cast. If the target does not have the spell you chose, another spell of the same rank or the nearest lower rank is chosen at random from the spells the creature can cast. If the spell is not a cantrip, you can Cast the Spell once before the end of your next turn without expending a spell slot. If the spell can only be cast a finite number of times, such as from spell slots, the creature loses one of these uses. If the spell you stole is a constant spell, the target retains the spell's effects even when you steal the spell.

Failure You fail to steal the spell.

Critical Failure Your attempt to tap into magic leads to an overwhelming rebuttal of energy. You become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 round.

Special If you are a wizard of the School of Unified Magical Theory, the first time you use Steal Spell on a target each day they do not become temporarily immune.

Larcenomancy.name: Larcenomancy
Larcenomancy.description:
That magic is a resource to be taken from the unworthy

Those that would deal in the treachery of theft take that which does not belong to them, but what is magic if not the property of those that wield the arcane? Larcenomancers, or spell-thieves, are wizards which argue that there is nothing inherently immoral about harnessing the magic of others to cast your own spells. It is far worse to witness a fool attempt a spell with bungling flourishes and amateur pronunciation than to place the ownership of such magic in its rightful hands. Spell-thieves from the School of Dwimmeric Entertainment often busy themselves in con-artistry and scams which lead to people willingly handing over their belongings (and sometimes, their spells), while spell-thieves who have studied the School of the Boundary might concert their energy in uncovering ancient horrors and harnessing their power through illgotten means.

Your deliberation skill is Thievery. When you attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Q5iIYCFdqJFM31GW]{Learn a Spell} from another caster, a scroll, or a spellbook, your Learn a Spell activity loses the concentrate trait and gains the manipulate trait and you must be able to touch the source of your learning. If you successfully Learn a Spell this way, the magical writings disappear or the caster loses the ability to Cast that Spell until 1 day has passed.

Your intrinsic bond to magic is through thieving abilities, deft maneuvers, a set of special gloves, or other trappings by which you capture magic. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-wizards.wizards-misc.iGVlBqHGCbvHnNb5]{Steal Spell} action.

Divest Soul.name: Divest Soul
Divest Soul.description:
You leverage lingering magic to make deceased creatures fight on your behalf. Choose a living creature within 30 feet that is at least dying 2 or the corpse of a once-living creature within 30 feet. You produce either a corpse or phantasm, chosen at the time you use Divest Soul. If you Divest Soul on a living creature to produce a corpse, it dies and Divest Soul gains the death trait. If you Divest Soul on a living creature to produce a phantasm, the effect ends immediately if the creature you targeted regains consciousness.

The corpse or phantasm’s level is a level no greater than your level – 2 or the level of the creature you targeted, whichever is lower. It has the minion trait and gains 2 actions for the turn when you use Divest Soul or when you Sustain this effect. The creature remains under your control for 1 minute, after which the effect ends. Regardless of the result, you cannot target the same creature or corpse with Divest Soul for 1 day. If you use Divest Soul again while the effect is active, any previous effect immediately ends.

Minions created with Divest Soul have void healing and are immune to bleed, death effects, disease, mental, paralyzed, poison, and unconscious and are automatically destroyed at 0 Hit Points. They have a Speed of 25 feet, a number of Hit Points equal to 5 x its level (minimum of 5 Hit Points), weakness to vitality damage equal to 5 plus its level, and its AC is equal to 10 plus its level plus your intelligence modifier and its saves are equal to its level plus your Intelligence modifier. It uses your spell attack modifier for its Strikes and Athletics checks but retains no other abilities or skills from its previous life. If the creature is at least 4th level, its Strikes deal an additional die of damage, two additional damage dice if it is at least 10th level, or three additional dice if it is at least 16th level. Minions you create with Divest Soul do not count towards your total minions.

Corpse The creature has the undead trait and a resistance to cold, electricity, fire, piercing, and slashing equal to 2 plus half its level. Its claw Strikes deal 1d6 piercing damage plus half your Intelligence modifier and have the agile trait.

Phantasm The creature has the spirit trait and floats off the ground, and is immune to difficult terrain and greater difficult terrain. It has resistance to all damage equal to 1 plus half your Intelligence modifier (except force and vitality), or 1 plus your Intelligence modifier if it is at least 10th level. Its ghostly hand Strikes deal 1d4 spirit damage plus half your Intelligence modifier.

Special If you are a wizard of the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classfeatures.xYYhJtGhFSWNifcO]{School of Unified Magical Theory}, you can have a number of corpses under your command from Divest Soul equal to 1 plus half the highest rank spell you can cast.

Planar Tradition.name: Planar Tradition
Planar Tradition.description:
When you first select this archetype, you choose a tradition other than arcane to be your planar tradition for quasiplanar casting. During your daily preparations you choose two planes associated with your planar tradition as your studied planes, or three planes if you are at least 11th level. When you cast the quasiplanar flux focus spell you create a flux connection to one of your studied planes. You gain additional spell slots that can be used to Cast a Spell when a flux is open. The spell repertoire for fusion spells depends on the flux and you can only cast the fusion spells while quasiplanar flux is active. At first level, you can cast one 1st-rank fusion spell per day and one cantrip fusion spells. You must have the spell in your planar spell repertoire to cast it; this is a collection of spells granted to you depending on the plane chosen for the flux. Any of these spells that aren’t normally on the arcane list are still arcane spells if you cast them this way. As you increase in level, you gain further fusion spell slots, and your quasiplanar casting grants you higher-rank fusion spells, even eventually granting you access to multiple fluxes at once. When you have multiple fluxes active, you treat all the spells associated with the flux as spells in your spell repertoire for your fusion spells.

Stance: Arcane Vitalization.name: Stance: Arcane Vitalization
Stance: Arcane Vitalization.description:
You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier. The only Strikes you can make are force punch unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 force damage; are in the brawling group; and have the force, parry, shove, trip, and unarmed traits. Alternatively, you can make ranged force punch unarmed attacks out to a range of 30 feet that deal 1d4 force damage with the force, propulsive, and unarmed traits. Both of these unarmed attacks use your spell attack modifier instead of your unarmed attack modifier.

While in Arcane Vitalization, you gain a +3 item bonus to AC and a +1 circumstance bonus to any defenses against being Shoved or Tripped. However, you have a Dexterity modifier cap to your AC of +1, and your Speeds are all reduced by 5 feet. The item bonus to AC from Arcane Vitalization is cumulative with armor potency runes on your explorer's clothing or cloth armors, mystic armor, and bracers of armor.

Effect: Compressed Spell.description: If your next action is to Cast a Spell that affects a burst, cone, or line, has no duration, and requires a save, you can alter the spell area to instead target a single creature that would be within the area of effect and the creature takes a –2 status penalty to its save against the spell.
